title: On the global well-posedness for the nonlocal Fokas-Lenells equation with the weighted Sobolev initial data on the line
authors: Zhenya Yan, Guoqiang Zhang, Guancheng Zhu
abstract: We establish the global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the reverse space-time nonlocal Fokas-Lenells equation with the weighted Sobolev initial data $q_0(x)\in H^{3}(\mathbb{R}) \cap H^{2,1}(\mathbb{R})$ on the line. We develop the inverse scattering transform formulated via the associated Riemann-Hilbert problems to study this issue. A spectral uniformization transform is introduced to resolve the singular behavior inherent in the KN-type negative flow spectral problem. Owing to the reverse space-time reduction, reflection coefficients no longer satisfy the usual Hermitian conjugation symmetry, and the coercivity of the jump matrix is therefore not available a priori. The quantitative smallness condition on the initial data yields uniform bounds on the reflection coefficients and ensures the uniform positive definiteness of the Hermitian part of the associated jump matrix. The resulting coercivity allows us to establish the bounded invertibility of the associated singular integral operator through a Fredholm and vanishing-lemma argument. Under this condition, we prove an $L^{2}$-Sobolev bijective correspondence between the potential and scattering data, exclude spectral singularities on continuous spectra, and obtain the global existence and uniqueness of solutions. Moreover, the associated solution map is Lipschitz continuous on the admissible initial-data class.
summary: This paper proves the global well-posedness for the nonlocal Fokas-Lenells equation using an advanced Inverse Scattering Transform approach. The methodology involves solving associated Riemann-Hilbert problems and overcoming technical hurdles related to non-standard symmetries in the spectral problem. The result confirms that unique solutions exist globally in time, which is crucial for modeling physical systems like optical pulse propagation.
main_problem: The primary goal is establishing the global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the reverse space-time nonlocal Fokas-Lenells (nFL) equation on the line.
main_result: Global existence and uniqueness of solutions are proven, and the associated solution map is shown to be Lipschitz continuous on the admissible initial-data class.
method: The analysis heavily relies on developing an Inverse Scattering Transform (IST) framework formulated via associated Riemann-Hilbert (RH) problems and utilizing spectral uniformization transforms.
model_or_system: The model is the nonlocal Fokas-Lenells equation, $q_{xt} - q + iqq^{PT} = 0$, which generalizes integrable models like NLS and is relevant to modeling ultrashort optical pulses in nonlinear media.
key_observables: The potential $q(x, t)$, reflection coefficients ($r_j$), and the associated scattering data are key observables used throughout the analysis.
important_parameters: Weighted Sobolev initial data regularity: $q_0(x) \in H^3(\mathbb{R}) \cap H^{2,1}(\mathbb{R})$, and a quantitative smallness condition on the initial data is required for technical steps.
main_assumptions: The proof requires establishing uniform bounds on reflection coefficients by assuming a smallness condition on the initial potential, which ensures positive definiteness of the Hermitian part of the jump matrix.

paper_structure: The paper follows a standard IST approach: defining the direct scattering problem, constructing associated Riemann-Hilbert problems, developing the necessary transforms (like spectral uniformization), proving global reconstruction via controlled singular integral operators, and finally establishing the Lipschitz continuity of the solution map.
why_interesting: While focused on nonlinear PDEs rather than quantum dynamics directly, the use of advanced spectral methods (IST/RH problems) to prove long-time existence is a powerful mathematical tool applicable to analyzing complex quantum field theories or open quantum systems governed by integrable Hamiltonians.
